read_comparators.title: Distance makes things look better
read_comparators.odia: ଦୂର ପର୍ବତ ସୁନ୍ଦର; ଦୂର ବନ୍ଧୁ ସୁନ୍ଦର
read_comparators.literal_meaning: A distant mountain is beautiful; a distant friend is beautiful.
read_comparators.explanation: Distance can hide the rough edges of a place or a relationship. What looks inviting from afar may feel different when we know its everyday difficulties. The saying gently questions an ideal picture; it does not claim that friendship needs distance.
read_comparators.meaning_odia: ଦୂରରୁ ପାହାଡ଼ର ଖାଲଢିପ ଦିଶେନାହିଁ; ଦୂରର ବନ୍ଧୁଙ୍କ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ଅସୁବିଧା ବି ଆଖିରେ ପଡ଼େନାହିଁ। ନିକଟରୁ ଜାଣିଲେ ଯେଉଁ ତଫାତ ଦିଶେ, କଥାଟି ତାହାକୁ ମନେ ପକାଏ। ଦୂରର ସୁନ୍ଦର ଛବିକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବା ଏହାର ଭାବ, ବନ୍ଧୁତା ଭଲ ରହିବା ପାଇଁ ଦୂରେଇ ରହିବା ଦରକାର ବୋଲି ନୁହେଁ।
read_comparators.usage_example: Someone envies a friend’s life from holiday photographs; a longer visit reveals ordinary chores and worries too. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
read_comparators.cultural_context: The dictionary gives two parallel images: a mountain seen from afar and a friend kept at a distance. This explanation is an editorial reading of that contrast, not an origin story.

read_comparators.explanation: The source applies the image to someone who attends to others while neglecting those close by. Light reaching outward does not mean every nearby place receives it.
read_comparators.meaning_odia: ଦୀପର ଆଲୁଅ ବାହାରକୁ ଯାଉଛି, ହେଲେ ତାହାର ପାଖରେ ଅନ୍ଧାର ରହିଯାଇଛି। ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ଏହା ଅନ୍ୟଙ୍କ ପ୍ରତି ଧ୍ୟାନ ଦେଇ ନିଜ ପାଖର ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଅବହେଳା କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର। ଦୂରର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ଦେଖିବା ସହ ନିକଟର ଅଭାବ ଆଖିରୁ ଖସିଯାଉଛି କି ନାହିଁ, ସେ କଥା ବି ଭାବିବାକୁ ହୁଏ।

read_comparators.title: Distance does not end a claim
read_comparators.literal_meaning: Even in the forest, the elephant belongs to the king.
read_comparators.explanation: The line presents a claim that persists despite distance. Applied figuratively, it can suggest that being out of sight does not by itself remove someone’s connection or responsibility.
read_comparators.meaning_odia: ହାତୀ ବଣରେ ଅଛି, ତଥାପି ତାହା ଉପରେ ରାଜାଙ୍କ ଦାବି ରହିଛି—ପଙ୍କ୍ତିଟି ଏହି ତଫାତକୁ ରଖେ। ଦୂରେ ରହିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ସମ୍ପର୍କ ବା ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଆପେ ଶେଷ ହୁଏନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଏକ ରୂପକ ଅର୍ଥ ନିଆଯାଇପାରେ। ଏହା ସୀମିତ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠ, ହାତୀ ଉପରେ କୌଣସି ଐତିହାସିକ ବା ବର୍ତ୍ତମାନର ଅଧିକାରର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
read_comparators.usage_example: Equipment lent to another office remains the lender’s responsibility to keep on its inventory. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
read_comparators.cultural_context: No source gloss accompanies the line. It is not used as evidence for any historical law giving a king ownership of all elephants.

read_comparators.title: When unclear words become scripture
read_comparators.literal_meaning: When Brahma speaks incoherently, it is the Veda.
read_comparators.explanation: The saying makes the speaker’s standing outweigh the clarity of the words. Even incoherent speech is received as scripture when it comes from Brahma. The dictionary places this example under the sense “to speak incoherently” and labels it a Dhaga. The further reading offered here is satirical: a statement can acquire authority merely because of who says it. That is an editorial interpretation of the contrast, not a doctrinal account of the Vedas.
read_comparators.meaning_odia: ବ୍ରହ୍ମା ବିଳିବିଳେଇଲେ ବି ତାହା ବେଦ। କଥା କେତେ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ, ତାହାଠାରୁ କିଏ କହୁଛି ସେ କଥା ବଡ଼ ହୋଇଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଅନର୍ଥକ ବାକ୍ୟ କହିବା ଅର୍ଥରେ ଏହି ଢଗଟି ଉଦାହରଣ ହୋଇଛି। ଏଠାରେ ଆମର ପାଠ ହେଉଛି ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦାର ଜୋର ଉପରେ ଏକ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ—ବଡ଼ ଲୋକ କହିଛନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଅସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କଥାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅଭ୍ରାନ୍ତ ଧରିନେବା।
read_comparators.english_summary: A speaker’s prestige can make unclear words seem authoritative.
read_comparators.odia_summary: କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦାରେ ଅସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କଥା ବି ପ୍ରମାଣ ହୋଇଯାଏ।
read_comparators.usage_example: A vague remark by a famous speaker is repeated as a firm rule, although nobody can explain what was meant. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
read_comparators.cultural_context: Brahma and the Veda remain the source’s cultural anchors. The dictionary supports the lexical sense and identifies the example as Dhaga; the prestige-over-clarity interpretation is Project Odisha’s reading. No originating scripture passage or religious teaching is asserted, and the saying is not attributed to Brahma as its author.

read_comparators.title: Leaving care at the gate
read_comparators.literal_meaning: Give the old bull coarse juannia grass; whether it eats or not, let it loose and come away.
read_comparators.explanation: The food is offered, but whether the old animal can use it is treated as no concern of the giver. The dismissive ending is the revealing part: doing something that resembles care becomes an excuse to stop caring about the outcome. The source defines the grass as coarse and tough; it does not give a separate figurative gloss. Our reading hears a picture of perfunctory attention, especially when someone’s needs have changed. Quoting it critically can draw attention to neglect rather than recommend the conduct it describes.
read_comparators.meaning_odia: ବୁଢ଼ା ବଳଦକୁ ମୋଟା କରଡ଼ା ଘାସ ଦେଇଦେଲେ, ହେଲେ ସେ ଖାଇପାରିଲା କି ନାହିଁ ସେଥିରେ ଆଉ ଧ୍ୟାନ ନାହିଁ। ମେଲି ଦେଇ ଚାଲିଆସିବାର ଶେଷକଥାରେ ଏହି ଅବହେଳା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ହୁଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଘାସକୁ ମୋଟା ଓ କରଡ଼ା ବୋଲି କହିଛି; ଅଲଗା ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥ ଦେଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଏହା କେବଳ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ସାରିଦେବା ଭଳି ଯତ୍ନର ଚିତ୍ର—ଯାହା ପାଇଁ ଦିଆଗଲା, ତାହାର କାମରେ ଲାଗିଲା କି ନାହିଁ ଦେଖାଗଲା ନାହିଁ। ଏହି ଅବହେଳାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରି କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିହୁଏ, ତାହାର ଅନୁକରଣ କରିବା ପାଇଁ ନୁହେଁ।
read_comparators.english_summary: An offer of care means little when no one checks whether it meets the recipient’s needs.
read_comparators.odia_summary: ଯତ୍ନ ନାଁରେ କିଛି ଦେଇଦେବା ଓ ତାହା କାମରେ ଲାଗୁଛି କି ନାହିଁ ଦେଖିବା ଏକ କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
read_comparators.usage_example: Original imagined example: A club sends a complicated online form to a member who has already said they cannot use that system. When someone says “We sent it, so our job is done,” another member quotes the saying to challenge that indifference and offers to help complete the form.
read_comparators.cultural_context: The analogy is read critically, not as animal-care advice or an assertion that older people have less value. The source spelling ଜୂଆଁଣିଆ in the quoted line is retained although the headword has ଜୁଆଁଣିଆ. No species or agricultural history is inferred.

read_comparators.title: A fine shawl and forgotten faces
read_comparators.literal_meaning: Is this the former Kahnei? With a fine soft shawl on the shoulder, does he recognise people?
read_comparators.explanation: The question contrasts a remembered person with the way he now behaves. The fine shawl becomes the visible sign beside a failure to recognise others. Our reading hears a teasing accusation that improved appearance or standing has brought social distance. The line does not tell us that the cloth itself changes character, or that everyone whose circumstances improve becomes proud. Its force is directed at the particular person being addressed through this pointed question.
read_comparators.meaning_odia: ଏ କି ସେଇ ପୂର୍ବର କହ୍ନେଇ—ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପୁରୁଣା ପରିଚୟ ଓ ଏବର ଆଚରଣ ମୁହାଁମୁହିଁ ହେଉଛି। କାନ୍ଧର ସରୁ କୋମଳ ଚାଦର ପାଖରେ ମଣିଷ ନ ଚିହ୍ନିବାର କଥା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ବେଶ ବା ସ୍ଥିତି ବଦଳିଲା ପରେ ପୁରୁଣା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଅବହେଳା କରିବା ଉପରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ପୋଷାକଟି ନିଜେ ଦୋଷୀ ନୁହେଁ; ତାହା ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା ଲୋକର ବ୍ୟବହାର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପଡ଼ୁଛି।
read_comparators.english_summary: A changed appearance becomes an image for forgetting familiar people.
read_comparators.odia_summary: ବେଶ ବଦଳିଲା ପରେ ପରିଚିତ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଭୁଲିବାରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
read_comparators.usage_example: Original imagined example: After a promotion, a friend stops greeting the people who used to share lunch with him. One of them quotes the saying in a private conversation, teasing the new distance rather than the friend’s clothes.
read_comparators.cultural_context: The source labels the headword Jajpur; no exclusive origin follows. Kahnei remains the name in the quotation, not an identified deity or historical person. Fine soft cloth is explicit; fibre, cost and status-history are not established. Source spelling ପୂରୂବ retained.

read_comparators.title: When lasting illness becomes invisible
read_comparators.literal_meaning: They do not look towards the chronically ill person.
read_comparators.explanation: The dictionary defines the person in the line as chronically ill. The statement records a harsh lack of attention, but its brief quotation gives no speaker or occasion to tell us whether the neglect was being observed, lamented or defended. Our reading uses it critically: a difficulty that lasts can cease to attract the attention given to a new crisis. That is a way to question neglect, not a reason to accept it or a claim that every family behaves this way.
read_comparators.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ “ନିତି ମଳୁ”ର ଅର୍ଥ ଦୀର୍ଘଦିନ ରୋଗରେ ପୀଡ଼ିତ ଲୋକ। ତାଙ୍କ ଆଡ଼କୁ ଚାହାନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ପଦଟି କଠୋର ଏକ ଅବହେଳା କହେ। କିଏ କେଉଁ ଭାବରେ କହିଥିଲେ, ଛୋଟ ଉଦ୍ଧୃତିରୁ ତାହା ଜଣାଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଆମେ ଏହାକୁ ଅବହେଳାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରି ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ: କଷ୍ଟଟି ବହୁଦିନ ରହିଲା ବୋଲି ତାହା ପ୍ରତି ଧ୍ୟାନ ଶେଷ ହୋଇଯିବ କାହିଁକି?

read_comparators.title: Start again for the headman
read_comparators.literal_meaning: When the headman arrives, sing from the beginning.
read_comparators.explanation: In our reading, a late arrival changes where the song must begin. Placed under “village headman,” the line brings authority into that restart. Our reading hears a teasing complaint: everyone else has already listened, but the important newcomer gets the beginning again. The dictionary supplies the role, not a documented performance custom or this modern meeting application.
read_comparators.meaning_odia: ଆସିଥିବା ଲୋକଟି ପାଇଁ ଗୀତ ପୁଣି ମୂଳରୁ ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୁଏ। ଅଭିଧାନର ଗ୍ରାମପ୍ରଧାନ ଅର୍ଥ ଏହି ପୁନରାରମ୍ଭରେ ପଦମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦାକୁ ଆଣେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଟିକେ ଟାହି ଅଛି—ଅନ୍ୟମାନେ ଶୁଣିସାରିଲେଣି, ତଥାପି ବଡ଼ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ପୁଣି ଆରମ୍ଭ! ଅଭିଧାନ ଭୂମିକାଟି ବୁଝାଏ; କୌଣସି ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ଗାୟନପ୍ରଥା ବା ଆଜିର ସଭାର ଉଦାହରଣ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
read_comparators.english_summary: Our reading hears a teasing restart for someone with authority.
read_comparators.odia_summary: ପଦମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦା ପାଇଁ ପୁଣି ଆରମ୍ଭ କରିବାର ଟାହି।
read_comparators.usage_example: Original imagined example: The chairperson joins after a club discussion has nearly finished and asks for the opening explanation again. A member quietly quotes the line to a neighbour, then offers a short recap. This is an invented application, not a recorded village practice.
read_comparators.cultural_context: The quotation belongs to the village-headman sense, separately from the headword’s family-title and military senses. It identifies no present caste, family or officeholder.

findings.finding: Proximity enables regular attention; differs from distance idealization and outward care neglecting nearby people. No settlement or yield prescription.
Explicit new attraction displacing old attention; distinct addressed complaint from shawl/status forgetting, perfunctory care or chronic-illness neglect. Relationships remain unspecified.
Unexpected appearance of rival/share claimant differs from king elephant ownership persisting at distance. No fraud, unearned claim or inevitable opposition asserted.

Ringed-hand slap valued as sacred bath is distinct from prestige making unclear speech scripture or headman prompting restart. Critical counterreading explicitly editorial, no traditional counter-moral or ritual-efficacy claim.
